first_impression.reaction: My assistant sent this as a quick reference, so I skimmed her summary and then the page. The opening is calm and not trying too hard: 'A place card is the smallest piece of stationery at your wedding and the one every guest picks up.' Fine. Nothing cheap on the first screen. But nothing tells me this team has ever set a table for 300 people either. It reads like a well-mannered ideas list, not a planner I'd brief.

journey.quote: These wedding place cards ideas are grouped by style, so you can shortlist in a minute: classic paper, natural and edible, keepsakes, glass and acrylic, local touches, and cards that sit on the napkin or plate.
journey.reaction: Good. Organised and quick. My assistant can pull two or three options from this without wasting my time.

journey.quote: Ask for a lettering sample on the actual card stock, as some inks feather on textured paper.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of detail that tells me someone has actually done this. Understated and useful.

journey.section: Keepsake Place Cards That Double as Favours
journey.quote: Shot glasses suit a lively reception.
journey.reaction: Not our wedding. Skipped it. Not offensive, just a reminder this page is written for everyone.

journey.section: How to Do Wedding Place Cards
journey.quote: Check titles such as Dr or Mr and Mrs, preferred names and every surname.
journey.reaction: At our table this is the part that actually matters: how senior family members and guests of standing are addressed. 'Dr or Mr and Mrs' feels like it was written for a suburban reception. It doesn't show me they understand forms of address beyond the basics.

journey.quote: Test a sample by candlelight: if it isn't legible at a glance, choose a bolder ink or a plainer script.
journey.reaction: Sensible. Older relatives will be squinting at calligraphy otherwise.

journey.section: Place Cards for a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Someone needs the plan, the cards and time before guests arrive. Agree whether that is the venue, your planner or your stylist.
journey.reaction: Right question, but at 200 to 400 guests this is a team job, not 'someone'. Nothing here acknowledges scale, which is the thing I'm actually shortlisting on.

journey.section: Place Cards for a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the venue, travel, vendors and payments, and works in your time zone.
journey.reaction: This is the only line that speaks to how I'd want to work. One person, my time zone. My assistant would flag it.

journey.quote: Send each stationer your chosen idea, the setting and the final name list from your seating plan, and ask to see a sample.
journey.reaction: Send our full guest list to every stationer we're comparing? No. That list is exactly what ends up somewhere it shouldn't. The directory framing also makes me feel like a self-service customer.

journey.section: Plan the table with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fine, it's discreet enough. I'd rather hear what's possible than about fees, but it isn't pushy.

unanswered_questions: Has this team handled place cards and seating at 200 to 400 guests? The page never says what changes at that size.
Who handles the guest list, and how is it kept private when it goes to stationers and vendors?
Can the Wedded Advisor work alongside my family office and my assistant, not just with me?
Is there a private way to start the conversation, or only the general Wedded Concierge page?

turn_offs_found.quote: Find a stationer on Wedded Marketplace, our directory of venues and vendors, and compare styles.
turn_offs_found.why: Directory and 'compare' language reads as self-service. It's the standard-client treatment I'm trying to avoid.

turn_offs_found.quote: Send each stationer your chosen idea, the setting and the final name list from your seating plan, and ask to see a sample.
turn_offs_found.why: Sharing the full guest list with several vendors before choosing one is a privacy risk for a family like ours.

would_share_with: My assistant, as a reference for the stylist brief

cta_reaction.quote: If the details are starting to stack up, talk to Wedded Concierge about the wider plan.
cta_reaction.why: The single point of contact in my time zone is the right promise, but I enquire through a referral or a private channel. A place card article alone won't get me to click; at most my assistant notes the name.

top_3_changes: Protect the guest list. Old: "Send each stationer your chosen idea, the setting and the final name list from your seating plan, and ask to see a sample." New: "Send each stationer your chosen idea and the setting, and ask to see a sample. Share the final name list from your seating plan only with the stationer you book."

Widen forms of address beyond the basics. Old: "Check titles such as Dr or Mr and Mrs, preferred names and every surname." New: "Check titles and honorifics, preferred names and every surname, and agree early how senior family members and guests of honour are addressed."

Acknowledge scale on the day. Old: "Someone needs the plan, the cards and time before guests arrive." New: "Someone needs the plan, the cards and time before guests arrive, and with a long guest list that can mean a small team working from the same plan."

Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, Dubai, assistant reads first, discretion-led)
No invented brand facts; gaps listed in unanswered_questions
Suggested edits use exact old strings from the draft and add no new facts, vendor names, fees, commissions or supplier vetting claims

Payload matches 07-icp.schema.json; top_3_changes has at most 3 items

open_questions.question: This is a high-volume ideas post, so low relevance for the UHNW persona may be acceptable. Should the guest-list privacy edit still be applied, given it costs nothing for other personas?

assumptions: Read in fast mode as the persona's assistant would surface it: a skim of the full page, not a close read.
Persona card is provisional and not CRM-calibrated, so reactions reflect the assumed profile.
